_meta.what: The squares and captions painted into the picture of the global map that go with places taken out of the game.
_meta.why: The full-scale map (res/globalmap/full/<n>.jpg, 273 tiles, one cell 8x8 pixels) has every place painted into the photograph itself: a coloured square on its cell and, for a few, a caption in letters. Hiding a place's name (data/map_labels.json) leaves its square, so a cut has to take the square off too.
_meta.rule: Every cell of data/retired.json 'cells' loses its square by itself: nothing to add here for a place that stood on a cell. 'cells' below are the other cells whose square goes -- a name with no place under it -- each with its why. 'captions' are letters painted into the picture, each as boxes of the map's pixels (x0, y0, x1, y1, inclusive; pixel = cell * 8) painted over whole. 'keep' lists cells whose name is hidden but whose square stays, each with its why: server/test_map_cells.py makes every hidden name with no live place under it be here, erased or bare. 'bare' lists cells whose name is hidden and whose picture has no square at all, each with its why: nothing is painted there, and server/test_map_cells.py holds the real map to that. 'paint' goes the other way: 'x,y' -> {colour, why}, a square painted on a cell that has none, for a place of ours (data/locations) put on the map; colour is one of server/map_cells.py's PALETTE (green, red, blue, black, white, orange, yellow, tan).
_meta.how: server/map_cells.py finds each square in the picture and paints it over with the photograph's texture from near by; only the JPEG blocks it touches are encoded anew. client/build.py puts the edited tiles into every client release, bootstrap_http serves them on a local run. To look at the result: python3 server/map_cells.py --res <res> --preview <folder>.
_meta.zones: A war zone painted round a place that is gone -- a circle tinted by 'tint' laid over the photograph, arrows over it -- is taken off before the squares are found: every pixel under the circle back to the photograph (its alpha the zone's own, else the tint's), the line on its rim measured and taken off where it is, the arrows' and seams' polygons (the map's pixels, painted over whole) painted over with the photograph from near by, less the squares and the letters ('letters', boxes of the map's pixels) painted over them. Nothing outside the zone's 'tiles' changes. Squares and letters a zone leaves may go after it all the same, as cells and captions (the villages' «Поселок» and the squares across the river, 2026-10-13): they are found and painted over on the picture without the zone.

tint.why: Measured on the four circles (server/map_cells.py clear_zones): pure red laid over the photograph at an alpha that is nothing within 61 pixels of the centre, rises evenly to its whole at 108 and so stays to the rim, the circle 245 pixels across, its edge 2 pixels soft. A pixel just inside the rim is its neighbour outside moved towards (255, 0, 0) by that alpha, on sand (dR +3, dG -18, dB -11) and on dark rock (dR +17, dG -3) alike, as laying a colour over does: a step added to every pixel would darken the rock as much as the sand, a colour multiplied in would leave the rock as it was. Each zone has its own alpha, 0.09-0.10, from its own rim; this one is for a zone without. The rim also carries a thin line, yellowish (blue down by up to 8) and darker to the lower right, light and greener to the upper left (luma up by up to 40, red down by up to 15), as if lit from there: map_cells measures it along the rim, against the ground either side of it (on the next tile where a circle comes to its tile's edge), and takes it off where it is.
